operations.detail: Fresh detailed contract, canonical HEAD, unclaimed ownership and absence of all five runtime outputs read back.
Queue consumer selection code verified to accept pickup_requested, scan all page queue roots and order lower numeric priority first; the retry5 queue remains priority -100 and ready for claim.
Current-day queue-selection debug remained absent and the latest MULTI_PAGE runtime status remained stale, confirming that no fresh queue scan evidence exists.
Persistent daemon loop audited; it is designed to restart scan workers after success or failure, so the stale runtime evidence is not a normal single-loop completion.
Scan-worker lock validation gap identified: an old lock without process_start_time could combine with a reused live PID and produce a false RUNNER_ALREADY_ACTIVE result.
Slot-local helper now validates scan lock scope, canonical repo root, instance id, process start time, actual StartTime and exact canonical scan-worker command.
Invalid or stale MULTI_PAGE lock is removed only when zero exact canonical scan-worker processes exist; any exact worker preserves the lock and recovery fails closed.
Helper destructive stops now use a bound Process object whose StartTime matches CIM CreationDate, aligning stale-daemon termination with watchdog generation safety.

Two helper expression defects were detected by remote readback before canonical repinning; corrected helper content passed local delimiter-balance validation without claiming a PowerShell runtime parser pass.
Final recovery chain remotely read back as helper 10120503, preflight 3276a158, bootstrap 7e90940a and watchdog ce0cb3c1; same attempt and no second runner preserved.
